doc.title: The global schema: where it ends and the plugins begin
doc.p: Step 1 of the lab's design (decision pending: global schema plus one schema per plugin, approach A of lab/approaches.py). For every concept: whether the global schema holds it, from which engines have it. The evidence is the concept map (lab/concepts.py) over nine servers (MySQL 5.7, 8.0, 8.4, 9.7; PostgreSQL 14 to 18); Iceberg, Snowflake and BigQuery are checked from what they document. The rule: the global schema holds what people, the agent, the canvas and the rules use across databases, always optional where an engine may lack it; anything one engine alone has, or that changes how one engine stores or runs, is its plugin's.

list.item: engine_mysql: storage engines and table options, character sets, column on update, srid, invisible columns and indexes, prefix lengths, subpartitions, program context (definer, sql mode, character sets), event details, view algorithm and check option.

engine_postgresql: user-defined types (enum, composite, domain, range), policies, rules, extensions, collations, inheritance, persistence, storage options (fillfactor, autovacuum), index include, nulls order, operator classes, nulls not distinct, exclusion constraints, routine volatility, strictness, parallel safety and settings, trigger level and transition tables, deferrable constraints' validation.

Iceberg, Snowflake and BigQuery, checked on paper: each fits the global schema without adding to it; what they add (transforms, clustering, table properties, time travel, search indexes, row access policies) is theirs.
